label: Person
name: Agostinho José Sartori
summary:
Agostinho José Sartori (b. 1944) is a Brazilian Catholic bishop who has served in the Diocese of Caxias do Sul in Rio Grande do Sul state, a region of southern Brazil with an exceptionally strong Italian immigrant Catholic culture. Ordained a priest of the local diocese, he rose to episcopal leadership within the community he had always served.

Caxias do Sul sits in the Serra Gaúcha, the highland region of Rio Grande do Sul colonised primarily by Italian immigrants from the late nineteenth century. This community maintained extraordinarily intense Catholic practice: high Mass attendance, strong devotion to the Madonna, extensive parish associations, and deep integration of Catholic identity with Italian-Brazilian cultural life. Sartori's episcopal ministry engaged a community of unusual Catholic vitality by twentieth-century Western standards.

His episcopate navigated the tensions between traditional Catholic culture and the forces of secularisation that increasingly affected even the strongly Catholic southern Brazilian communities. As a bishop formed within this culture, he brought intimate local knowledge to his pastoral work, representing the successful development of indigenous episcopal leadership in a community that had historically relied on Italian missionary clergy.
